h1: Selling craft beer gift packs to companies: packaging and brand angles
title: Craft Beer Gift Packs for Companies | Craft Beer School
desc: How a brewery can sell craft beer gift packs to companies in India: what corporate buyers want, packaging, co-branding, rules and planning for festive peaks.
teaser: Corporate gifting can fill a brewery's festive order book, if the packs reach the buyer's desk before their deadline.
standfirst: Indian companies spend heavily on gifts at Diwali and year end. Craft beer is a growing request. Here is how to package and brand a corporate gift pack that buyers choose and recipients remember.
sections:
A corporate gift is chosen by one person and received by many. The buyer, usually in HR, admin or a founder's office, cares about a few practical things: it looks premium, it arrives on time, it fits the budget, it reflects well on the company and it does not cause trouble. The recipient cares whether it is good and whether it feels personal.

For craft beer, "does not cause trouble" matters most. Many companies have policies on gifting alcohol. Some recipients do not drink. A brewery that understands this wins repeat orders.

Alcohol cannot be shipped freely in India. Sale must usually happen through licensed channels. Moving beer across state lines needs permits that are often impractical for small gift orders. Rules on home delivery and gifting vary by state and change. Before you market a gift pack, work out with a licensing consultant how a company in your state can legally buy it and how it can reach recipients. That might mean delivery only within the state, sale through a licensed retailer partner or collection from your taproom.

Many breweries offer a version without beer for recipients in other states or who do not drink: glassware, merchandise, a brewery tour voucher or an alcohol-free option. Our guide to craft beer gifts has ideas from the drinker's side.

• A rigid gift box or sturdy carton with inserts that hold cans or bottles firmly. Loose cans in a bag look like a supermarket purchase.
  • A tasting card explaining each beer in a line or two, with serving suggestions and food ideas.
  • A branded glass, which outlasts the beer and keeps your brand on someone's desk.
  • Space for a message from the company, printed or as a card.

Pack for Indian heat. A box sitting in a warm office lobby for a day can hurt hoppy beers. Favour beers that hold up well, such as lagers, stouts and malty ales, over delicate hazy IPAs. Tell the buyer to keep the packs cool.

Many companies want their logo on the gift. A sleeve or card with their logo, inside your branded box, gives them that without turning your pack into a promotional product. Put your brand on the beer and the box. Put theirs on the message. Agree artwork deadlines early, because corporate approvals are slow.

Avoid co-branding the beer label itself unless you are ready for label approval in your state, which can take time and cost money for a one-off.

Corporate gifting peaks before Diwali and at year end. Buyers start looking weeks earlier and want samples, quotes and delivery dates. Breweries that are still deciding on a box design in October miss the season. Our guide to festive season beer marketing covers planning the whole period.

A real brewery-floor constraint: gift packs mean packaging runs, boxing and labelling all at the busiest time of year. Plan brewing and packing capacity months ahead. Order boxes early, because printers are busy too.

Make it easy to buy. A simple one-page offer with pack options, minimum order quantities, lead times, delivery areas and how payment and invoicing work suits corporate buyers. Have a sample pack ready to send. Follow up after the season with a thank you and a note about next year.

Price the pack from its full cost, not the beer alone. Boxes, inserts, cards, glassware, packing labour, delivery and any retailer margin can add up to more than the beer inside. Work out the cost per pack at two or three order sizes, then set clear tiers. Buyers like choice. Tiers stop you discounting a small order to the same rate as a large one.

Keep a short list of every company that bought, who signed off and what they chose. Corporate buyers change jobs often, so the contact who loved your pack this Diwali may be at a new company next year with a fresh budget.

Keep every message responsible. Present the gift as something to enjoy and share, with non-drinkers included.
faqs: Can a brewery deliver beer gift packs to offices in another state?
Usually not easily, because moving alcohol across state lines needs permits. Check with a licensing consultant and offer a non-alcohol version for other states.
When should we start selling Diwali corporate gift packs?
Start talking to buyers several weeks before the season, with samples and a clear offer. Plan packaging and production months ahead.
Should we put the client's logo on the beer label?
Usually it is simpler to put their logo on a sleeve or card. Changing the label itself may need fresh approval in your state.
